DISCRIMINATING: 'Phytophthora' vs 'Diaporthe'
Ruling feature : Location and appearance of stem lesion: dark brown basal lesion extending from the taproot upward (Phytophthora) vs. reddish-brown lesions at nodes in the lower canopy with sunken gray-brown cankers or linear rows of black pycnidia (Diaporthe)
Phytophthora: A dark brown lesion originating at the taproot and extending upward on the lower stem, capable of girdling the stem; associated with damping off, stunting, and yellowing.
Diaporthe: Small reddish-brown lesions near nodes in the lower third of the canopy expanding into sunken gray-brown cankers with reddish margins, and/or linear rows of black specks (pycnidia) on mature stems.
Decision rule  : IF the stem lesion is dark brown, originates at or near the taproot, and extends upward girdling the base, THEN suspect Phytophthora; IF lesions are reddish-brown at nodes forming sunken cankers with reddish margins OR linear rows of black specks appear on mature stems, THEN suspect Diaporthe.

DISCRIMINATING: 'Bacterial_Blight' vs 'Phytophthora'
Ruling feature : Location of primary symptoms: leaf lesions (angular, reddish-brown with yellow halo) vs. dark brown lower stem/taproot lesion
Bacterial_Blight: Small, angular, reddish-brown lesions with yellow halos on leaves, starting in the upper canopy on young leaves; older lesion centers fall out giving a tattered appearance.
Phytophthora: Dark brown lesion on the lower stem extending upward from the taproot, potentially girdling the stem and causing damping off, stunting, or plant death.
Decision rule  : IF the primary damage is angular leaf lesions with yellow halos and a tattered appearance, THEN it is Bacterial Blight (A); IF the primary damage is a dark brown lesion on the lower stem extending up from the taproot with possible stem girdling, THEN it is Phytophthora (B).

DISCRIMINATING: 'Bacterial_Blight' vs 'Diaporthe'
Ruling feature : Linear rows of black specks (pycnidia) on stems vs. angular leaf lesions with yellow halos
Bacterial_Blight: Small, angular, reddish-brown leaf lesions surrounded by a yellow halo, often coalescing into large dead areas; older lesion centers may fall out giving a tattered appearance, starting in the upper canopy on young leaves.
Diaporthe: Characteristic linear rows of black specks (pycnidia) on mature stems for pod and stem blight, or sunken gray-brown cankers with reddish margins near nodes in the lower canopy for stem canker; interior of lower stems may show thin black 'zone' lines.
Decision rule  : IF symptoms are primarily on leaves as angular lesions with a distinct yellow halo, THEN suspect Bacterial Blight (Disease A); IF symptoms are on stems with linear rows of black specks (pycnidia) or sunken cankers with reddish margins near nodes, THEN suspect Diaporthe (Disease B).
